function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates, 35 mph on rural non‑interstate roads, 25 mph in school zones.
• Commercial vehicles may have lower limits (e.g., 45 mph on rural interstates). | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• No “seat‑belt law” for drivers over 18, but failure to buckle can lead to a fine if the driver is pulled over. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use is prohibited for all drivers (including texting).
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for drivers 21+.
• Lower limits for commercial drivers (0.04%) and drivers under 21 (0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has the right‑of‑way.
• Stop signs and traffic signals must be obeyed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.003 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Drivers must not pass a stopped school bus until the bus’s stop sign is retracted. | Texas Transportation Code §545.004 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals at least 100 ft before changing lanes.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | Texas Transportation Code §545.005 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, 15 ft of a stop sign, or 10 ft of a fire hydrant.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited. | Texas Transportation Code §545.006 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection (except some exempt categories). | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage.
• Proof of insurance must be carried in the vehicle. | Texas Insurance Code §151.001 | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles: helmet required for riders under 18; helmets for all riders over 18.
• Commercial trucks: must follow specific weight and size limits. | Texas Transportation Code §545.007 | | **Emergency Vehicle Exemptions** | • Police, ambulance, and fire trucks may exceed speed limits and ignore certain traffic signals when responding to emergencies. | Texas Transportation Code §545.008 | ### How to Stay Updated 1. **TxDOT Website** – Regular updates on road conditions, speed limit changes, and construction projects. 2. **TxDMV** – For registration, insurance, and driver’s license information. 3. **Texas Legislature Online** – Access the Texas Transportation Code and any recent amendments. 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific traffic violation penalties and court procedures. --- #### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a simple habit that saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – put your phone on “Do Not Disturb” mode while driving. - **Observe speed limits** – they’re designed for safety, not convenience. - **Be mindful of school zones** – speeds drop significantly and children are present. - **Check your insurance** – ensure you meet the minimum liability requirements. If you need more detailed information on a particular law or want to check the latest statutes, let me know!
